text:
marta: Heads up — Prometheus scrape 95th latency spiked on us-west-gpu last night. Targets jumped from ~2500 -> 9k and scrapes started timing out.

alex: saw that too. many targets were the gpu-agent on nodes returning ~1.8M series each. prometheus logs: `scrape_duration_seconds > 20s` for dcgm/node exporters.

ravi: is this the per-GPU label explosion we saw before? which exporter is returning per-allocator labels?

marta: looks like the new runtime-metrics agent we rolled last week. it emits metrics per `gpu_uuid` + `process_id` + `cuda_context` — that exploded cardinality on machines running many tiny jobs.

kelsey: ouch. storage and egress costs are already up for the cluster. we need a short-term relabeling fix and a longer-term agent change.

alex: short-term: add metric_relabel_configs to drop `process_id` and `cuda_context` and aggregate by gpu_uuid only. e.g.:
```
metric_relabel_configs:
  - source_labels: [__name__]
    regex: 'runtime_.*'
    action: keep
  - source_labels: [process_id,cuda_context]
    action: labeldrop
```
This will lower series per-scrape.

marta: also increase scrape_timeout for the prometheus gpus job to `15s` and stagger scrapes with `scrape_interval: 30s` for the GPU job to reduce concurrent pressure.

prometheus-bot: alert: TSDB WAL pressure on prometheus-us-west-1 at 2026-02-12T03:47:12Z — retention spikes observed.

ravi: longer-term: patch the runtime-agent to emit aggregated metrics `gpu_utilization_total{gpu_uuid}` and `gpu_process_count{gpu_uuid}` instead of per-process gauges. We can add a feature flag.

kelsey: can we canary the relabel change via ServiceMonitor override in a single node pool? i.e., patch the k8s servicemonitor for node-exporter on `nodepool-gpu-canary` first.

marta: yes. example patch:
```
kubectl -n monitoring patch servicemonitor node-exporter-gpu -p '{"spec": {"endpoints": [{"interval": "30s","metricRelabelings": [{"action":"labeldrop","regex":"process_id|cuda_context"}] }]}}'
```

alex: i'll create the patch and roll to `nodepool-gpu-canary` after 10pm PST. will monitor for scrape_errors and series_count metric.

deploy-bot: deploy started: servicemonitor/node-exporter-gpu -> monitoring (canary) by alex @1779001200

kelsey: also worth adding a promql-based gauge to detect high-cardinality generators: `count by (job) (count({job=~".*gpu.*"}) by (__name__)) > 10000`

marta: thanks. once canary looks good we'll push a runtime-agent patch to reduce emitted label dimensions. follow-up doc: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-metrics-cardinality (draft)

alex: i'll post the rollout timeline in #eng-oncall once it's scheduled. :thumbsup:
